elements.element: Customer owns every Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 instead states that Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all other work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: No operative language gives Customer ownership of work product; Section 14.2 gives Vendor ownership of Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer its rights in Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: There is no assignment to Customer; the clause preserves Vendor ownership and grants only a licence.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 provides that Vendor retains Vendor Technology, and the added language confirms Vendor ownership of its generic tools and know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to any Vendor IP embedded in a Deliverable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 applies a licence under Section 13.2 to Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 expressly describes the incorporated-Vendor-Technology licence under Section 13.2 as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Although the added Deliverable licence is irrevocable, Section 14.3 separately governs incorporated Vendor Technology through Section 13.2, whose licence is described here only as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The added Deliverable licence is royalty-free, but Section 14.3 does not establish that the separate Section 13.2 licence covering incorporated Vendor Technology is royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no operative provision addressing ownership of or rights in Customer Data.

elements.element: The agreement does not create joint ownership of Deliverables, work product, Vendor IP, or Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The clause creates no joint ownership and expressly uses exclusive or retained Vendor ownership for the IP categories it addresses.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly states that Vendor owns its generic tools.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly states that Vendor owns its know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly grants Customer a licence to each Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer's Deliverable licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The added clause makes the licence perpetual and expressly disapplies the Order Form term limitation.

elements.element: Customer's Deliverable licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly makes the licence irrevocable and disapplies the revocable limitation.

elements.element: Customer's Deliverable licence is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly makes the licence worldwide.

elements.element: Customer's Deliverable licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly makes the licence royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly grants the right to use each Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer may modify each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly grants the right to modify each Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly grants the right to sublicense each Deliverable and disapplies the non-transferable limitation.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its Deliverable licence for its business.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly permits the licensed activities for Customer's business.

result.reason: The operative addition fully implements the fallback by preserving Vendor ownership of generic tools and know-how while granting Customer the required perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free rights to use, modify, and sublicense Deliverables for its business. It does not achieve the preferred position because Vendor still exclusively owns Deliverables, no assignment or Customer Data ownership language is included, and the separate embedded-Vendor-Technology licence is not shown to be irrevocable or royalty-free. The change is targeted and expressly neutralizes the conflicting licence limitations, though the coexistence of the Deliverable licence and the Section 13.2 embedded-technology licence leaves some scope ambiguity.
